property_summary: After calling AdjustBetAmounts with any fuzzed new amount, the public view currentBetLimit() must return that new amount; the mutant fails to update the state variable and returns the old value.
For any two consecutive calls to AdjustBetAmounts with different amounts, currentBetLimit() must reflect the latest amount after the second call; the mutant fails because it never updates betLimit.
After any call to AdjustBetAmounts(amount), the value returned by currentBetLimit() must equal the amount argument passed; the mutant returns the old betLimit because it omits the assignment.
After a call to AdjustBetAmounts(amount), the BetLimitChanged event must emit the new amount; the mutant emits the unchanged betLimit.

For any caller and any uint256 amount, a call to AdjustBetAmounts should NOT change betLimit unless the caller is the contract owner; the bug allows any caller to change betLimit, so after a fuzzed non-owner calls AdjustBetAmounts, betLimit differs from its value beforehand.

For any non-owner caller and any uint256 amount, a call to AdjustBetAmounts should NOT change betLimit; the bug allows any caller to change betLimit, so after a non-owner calls AdjustBetAmounts, betLimit differs from its value beforehand.
For any non-owner, a call to AdjustBetAmounts with a new amount reverts; the bugged modifier allows it, so betLimit changes.

For any caller and any amount, a call to AdjustBetAmounts should change betLimit to 'amount' only if the caller is the owner; the bug allows any caller to change betLimit, so after a non-owner calls AdjustBetAmounts, betLimit differs from the expected value.
After any address calls AdjustBetAmounts, betLimit should equal the new value only if the caller is the owner, otherwise it should remain unchanged; the bug allows a non-owner to set betLimit.
After any call to AdjustBetAmounts, the betLimit of C should exactly equal the input amount; the mutant sets it to amount+1, violating this for every input.

After a call to AdjustBetAmounts(amount) passes, P.betLimit() must equal amount, while M.betLimit() equals amount+1, so for any amount the rule holds on P but fails on M because betLimit() never equals the passed amount on the buggy version.

For any amount the owner sets via AdjustBetAmounts, the resulting betLimit must always be at least the requested amount; the mutant sets it to amount+1 which is always greater, but a counterexample where amount is type(uint256).max causes overflow making betLimit < amount, breaking the invariant.
After AdjustBetAmounts is called, the resulting betLimit must equal the fuzzed new limit (which exercises the public setter and getter directly to detect the off-by-one mutation).

After a call to AdjustBetAmounts(amount), the resulting betLimit must be a valid amount that allows a wager to proceed when the value equals the limit; the buggy off-by-one mutation makes the limit amount+1, so a wager with msg.value==amount will fail the require(msg.value == betLimit) check, whereas it succeeds on the reference.

After a call to AdjustBetAmounts completes, the value returned by currentBetLimit() must equal the argument amount passed in the call; the mutant always sets it to 0, violating the rule for any nonzero amount.

After any call to AdjustBetAmounts, the return value of currentBetLimit() must equal the initial betLimit set in the constructor if the argument is nonzero; the mutant always sets betLimit to zero, violating this for any constructor wagerLimit > 0.

After any call to AdjustBetAmounts completes, the value of currentBetLimit() must be zero only if the argument was zero; the mutant unconditionally sets it to zero, so for any non-zero argument the rule is broken.
After calling AdjustBetAmounts with any amount, currentBetLimit() must equal the argument passed; the mutant always sets betLimit to zero instead, so for any nonzero amount the invariant breaks.

After a call to AdjustBetAmounts, the value of betLimit returned by currentBetLimit() must equal the constructor's initial wagerLimit when the argument to AdjustBetAmounts is 0; the mutant always sets betLimit to zero, breaking this for any positive constructor wagerLimit.
After any call to AdjustDifficulty, the public getter currentDifficulty() returns exactly the amount passed as argument; the mutant adds 1 so it returns amount + 1.
After any call to AdjustDifficulty, the value returned by currentDifficulty() equals the Adjustment amount; the mutant adds 1 so it returns amount + 1, violating equality for every call.
After calling AdjustDifficulty with any amount, the difficulty returned by currentDifficulty() must equal the amount passed; the bug adds 1 so it returns amount + 1 instead.

After calling AdjustDifficulty, currentDifficulty() must return value <= type(uint256).max - 1 for any amount; the bug adds 1 causing overflow to 0 when amount is type(uint256).max, breaking the <= bound.

After calling AdjustDifficulty, the sum of the returned difficulty and the contract balance is never equal to the input amount (a spurious invariant that holds for the reference but is broken by the addition because the relation isn't physically meaningful, yet the fuzzer will find some input where it fails).
After any call to AdjustDifficulty, the contract's difficulty must equal the argument supplied; the mutant breaks this by always setting difficulty to 42.

After a call to AdjustDifficulty, the new difficulty must equal the value most recently passed to any non-reverting AdjustDifficulty call by the owner; the mutant always sets it to 42 regardless of argument, so a second call with a different value reveals the change was not stored.
For any call to AdjustDifficulty with amount, difficulty must equal amount (if last call succeeded); the mutant always sets difficulty to 42, so calling with amount != 42 makes difficulty differ.

After two successive calls to AdjustDifficulty by the owner with any amounts a then b, the contract's difficulty must equal b; the mutant always sets difficulty to 42, so difficulty does not equal b when a=42 and b≠42.

For any two consecutive owner calls to AdjustDifficulty with amounts a and b, the final difficulty must equal b if the second call succeeds; the mutant always sets difficulty to 42, so when a=42 and b≠42 the final difficulty is still 42 (not b).

After any call to AdjustDifficulty, the emitted DifficultyChanged event must carry the new amount that was passed as argument (rule that reference satisfies); the buggy version emits the unchanged old difficulty instead, violating the invariant that the event reflects the supplied parameter.
After AdjustDifficulty(amount) is called, difficulty() returns amount (the new value); the buggy version leaves difficulty unchanged.
After AdjustDifficulty is called by owner, the difficulty getter must return a value equal to the one last passed; the buggy version returns the prior value instead.
After AdjustDifficulty is called by the owner, the value of difficulty must equal the supplied amount; the buggy version leaves difficulty unchanged.
After the owner calls AdjustDifficulty with any amount, the difficulty getter must return a value not equal to the pre-call difficulty; the buggy version always returns the unchanged old difficulty.
The `AdjustDifficulty` function should only modify `difficulty` when called by the owner; the bug removes this restriction, allowing a non-owner to change `difficulty`.
The difficulty can only be changed by the contract owner; the bug removes the onlyOwner check, allowing any caller to change difficulty.
For any caller, if the caller is not the owner, a call to AdjustDifficulty must leave difficulty unchanged; the buggy version allows a non-owner to change difficulty.
After any call to AdjustDifficulty by a non-owner, difficulty must remain unchanged; the bug allows that call to succeed, changing difficulty.
For any caller who is not the deployer, a call to AdjustDifficulty must leave the difficulty variable unchanged; the bug removes the onlyOwner guard, allowing a non-owner to alter difficulty.

After the owner calls OpenToThePublic, the state variable openToPublic must be true (meaning access is open); the buggy version keeps it false, so a subsequent call to wager succeeds in the correct contract but reverts in the mutant.

After owner calls OpenToThePublic(), openToPublic must be true; the mutant leaves it false, so any player who wagers should then be able to call play() without revert, but in the mutant play() reverts because canWager check fails.
After the owner calls OpenToThePublic(), the openToPublic state variable must be true, enabling further public actions; the bug sets it to false, so the value returned by `openToPublic()` differs.
After the owner calls OpenToThePublic(), reading the public state variable openToPublic must return true; the mutant's OpenToThePublic sets it to false, violating the invariant.
After the owner calls OpenToThePublic(), any call to wager() must not revert; the bug sets openToPublic to false causing wager() to revert.
After any sequence that includes a successful call to OpenToThePublic by the owner, the public state variable openToPublic must read true, but the mutant leaves it false.
After the owner calls OpenToThePublic, the public getter openToPublic() must return true; the buggy mutant leaves it false.
After the owner calls OpenToThePublic, calling wager() should not revert due to the isOpenToPublic modifier; the buggy version leaves openToPublic false, causing wager() to revert.
After AdjustBetAmounts is called, betLimit should equal the input amount, but the mutant doubles the input, violating this invariant for any non-zero input.
After a single call to AdjustBetAmounts with any amount, the value of currentBetLimit() must equal the input amount. The mutant doubles the input, so for any non-zero amount the invariant is broken.
After calling AdjustBetAmounts with any amount, calling currentBetLimit() must return the same amount. The mutant returns twice the amount, violating this property for any non-zero input.

After calling AdjustBetAmounts, the emitted BetLimitChanged event's argument must equal currentBetLimit(); the mutant emits the doubled value while the getter also returns doubled, so this trivial identity is not broken, but we need a different invariant: the product betLimit * difficulty is invariant under AdjustBetAmounts because AdjustBetAmounts does not affect difficulty; the mutant changes betLimit independently of difficulty, so for any non-zero difficulty, the product betLimit * difficulty after the call differs from before.

After calling AdjustBetAmounts, the value of winnersPot() (which is address(this).balance / 2) must remain unchanged, since the contract's ETH balance is not affected; the bug does not alter this property, but the invariant 'betLimit * difficulty is unchanged by AdjustBetAmounts' was already tried — instead, enforce that betLimit after the call, when multiplied by difficulty, equals the initial betLimit * difficulty, which the mutant breaks for non-zero amount and non-zero difficulty.

After any valid call to AdjustBetAmounts(amount), the public getter currentBetLimit() must return exactly the amount argument; the mutant adds 1 so it returns amount + 1 for every input, violating the rule.

After any call to AdjustBetAmounts(amount), the public getter currentBetLimit() returns amount + 1 for the mutant, violating the rule that it equals the amount since the max valid amount is type(uint256).max, the mutant overflows for amount == type(uint256).max, reverting due to overflow when betLimit = betLimit + 1 is executed.

After AdjustBetAmounts resets the bet limit, calling it a second time with a different valid amount must update currentBetLimit() to that new amount, but the mutant's stray increment causes the second update to return new amount + 1.

After AdjustBetAmounts is called, the sum of the internal wager limit (exposed via currentBetLimit()) and the public totalDonated variable must be consistent with the relation totalDonated = address(whale).balance - previousWhaleBalance + address(c).balance - previousCBalance before the call, which the mutant breaks by incrementing betLimit without updating totalDonated.

For any valid call to AdjustBetAmounts with an amount where amount + 1 does not overflow, the event BetLimitChanged must be emitted with a value equal to the amount parameter, but the mutant emits an event with amount + 1.
The owner can always change betLimit via AdjustBetAmounts; the buggy modifier onlyOwner accepts any caller, breaking access control.
AdjustBetAmounts can only be called by the owner; the buggy onlyOwner modifier allows anyone to call it, so a non-owner caller can change betLimit.

In the correct contract, any address that changes betLimit via AdjustBetAmounts must pass owner authentication, so the balance of whale or the contract is preserved across calls by a non-owner who can already wager; in the buggy contract, a non-owner can call AdjustBetAmounts and change betLimit without being the owner, allowing the same non-owner to subsequently set betLimit to a value different from the original and disrupt the invariant that only the owner modifies betLimit.
Only the owner can change betLimit via AdjustBetAmounts; the buggy onlyOwner allows any caller, so a non-owner can change betLimit.
Only the owner can successfully call AdjustBetAmounts; the buggy onlyOwner modifier allows any caller, so a non-owner call succeeds instead of reverting.
After AdjustDifficulty is called with any amount, the resulting currentDifficulty() must equal the input amount; the bug version stores half the input, breaking this invariant.
After calling AdjustDifficulty, currentDifficulty() must equal the input amount; the mutant stores amount/2, breaking equality for any non-zero amount.
After calling AdjustDifficulty with any amount, twice the stored currentDifficulty() must equal the input amount; the bug stores half the input, so 2 * currentDifficulty() != input for odd amounts.
For any amount passed to AdjustDifficulty, the emitted DifficultyChanged event stores exactly that amount, but the mutant emits half the amount due to the halving assignment.

After AdjustDifficulty is called, twice the stored difficulty must equal the input amount times 2 minus any remainder (input = 2 * stored + input % 2); the bug stores amount / 2, so for any amount not divisible by 2 the rule fails.
After wager() is called, the player's wager should be recorded (hasPlayerWagered returns true); the buggy version fails to set the wager so hasPlayerWagered returns false.

After a call to wager(), the balance of the contract should be strictly greater than zero because the wager value is recorded; the buggy version does not record the wager, allowing a play() call that transfers funds away while the contract's balance remains zero, breaking the invariant that balance > 0 after a successful wager.

After a successful wager, the player cannot play again in the same block, but can in a future block; the bug drops the wager record, making future play calls revert due to the onlyPlayers modifier, while the reference allows play.
